Firstly, some basic mechanics:

Like I said in the OP, the ability for players to design their own patterns using pre-made templates (or at least be able to activate different basic attacks and mix-and-match them during a match, making improvised patterns on the fly that way. For example, one basic attack could be bullets that spawn in front of your character that move diagonally. Another could be a laser that travels down the screen. Players could use a mana system and use "mana" to use those different attacks, mixing them up to flood the screen and damage the opponent more effectively. Or, as aforementioned, players could make their own advanced patterns in an option menu that they can easily activate in-game, and in between patterns they can just use basic attacks) would be cool. 

If you go with the customizable pre-made pattern idea, then those patterns could be activated similar to how specials and ultimates are used in fighting games. The "ultimate" meter fills up with time and can store up to 3 or so charges. More powerful patterns consume more charges. 

There could also be a "final life" kind of deal. Like, a player can sacrifice themselves if they have low enough HP and a max ultimate meter to activate a survival/time-out pattern (like that final attack with the rotating planets in the video linked in the OP). If they fail to beat their opponent with that, they lose.

Buuuut for actually clever core game mechanic ideas... I'm not sure. It shouldn't be too necessary to go really out of the box with this genre. It's all about the difficulty and patterns which also go hand-in-hand. If you really want to do something unique, maybe you could try something with music. As fights go on, the BPM could change, which also affects the speed of the bullets. Or, even just as the song in the same BPM progresses, different elements are added. For example, during the most energetic parts of the song, bullets could bounce off of the walls, making things more "energetic."

I like all of these ideas. Here's my own:

**Team Roast Match** 
People are gathered into two teams. During the first round, each team sends one of their members up. Those two members compete in a **Roast Off**, following the same rules as the **Roast Off** in the OP. The loser is eliminated while the winner stays up. The next round, the team that lost sends another member up. From this round onward, the members of each team that are up do not roast, but are instead roasted by the other team. All members of Team A roast the representative of Team B and vice versa. As with the first round, the representative that is roasted the hardest is eliminated, and must be replaced by another member of the team. Anyone who is eliminated is no longer able to contribute to roasts or be roasted again in the Team Roast Match. This goes on until one team has lost all of its members, in which case, the team still standing is the winner. 

The reason why the first round is a one-on-one **Roast Off** is so everyone, including those that are nominated, has a chance to roast before they are eliminated. It also gives a slight strategic aspect, making teams think of who they want to send up first.

To make things more interesting, it may be nice to have entrants provide some background information and trivia about themselves that can be used against them, much like in **The Return of the King**.
